ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a benzene ring bearing an ortho-hydroxy group, and the benzene ring is connected to a central enol/enone precursor fragment containing an oxygen anion; the oxygen below the center is labeled with a negative charge, and there is a curved arrow pointing to the carbon connected to it, indicating re-formation of the carbonyl. In the middle there is a C=C double bond, and a curved arrow goes from this double bond to the oxygen on the adjacent carbon on the right side; this carbon on the right side is also connected to a phenyl group and bears an OOH/oxygen-related group. Reasoning: According to the arrow pushing, the negatively charged oxygen pushes back to form C=O, giving a ketone carbonyl connected to the ortho-hydroxyphenyl group; meanwhile, the electrons of C=C form a C–O bond to the adjacent oxygen, causing the original two alkene carbons and oxygen to close into a three-membered epoxide ring. The phenyl group on the right side remains on the benzylic carbon of the epoxide ring, and the ortho-hydroxyphenyl group on the left side remains unchanged. Therefore the product is an α,β-epoxy ketone, whose SMILES is O=C(C1OC1c2ccccc2)c3c(O)cccc3.

Keep the right phenyl attached to the benzylic epoxide carbon and keep the left ortho phenol unchanged. Write the product as the α,β-epoxy ketone SMILES O=C(C1OC1c2ccccc2)c3c(O)cccc3.
